_README: #5079 (epic #5051, charter #5067): the FIXED training scorecard the /training-review block retro re-grades once per block (the block is the charter's rotation.anchors_fixed_weeks; the retro cadence is the charter's calibration.block_retro). Thirteen rows, copied from the owner-private elite-panel review of 2026-10-18 (the rows only: the review, and the grades it gave, stay private — the 2026-10-18 baseline letters are an owner-only DynamoDB row, never this file, because the repo is PUBLIC). Each row names the platform reads that grade it (`inputs`, keys of lambdas/training/block_retro.py's evidence) and, where code can score it, its `code_rules` (ADR-105: deterministic computation before any model verdict); the eight-seat panel re-grade (route charter.retro, one call per seat) scores every row, and lambdas/training/block_retro.py combines the two. Every training TARGET is read from config/training_charter.json at run time, never copied here. Hand-owned; a change is a new version with a change_log line. A grade below `grade_scale.fix_below` becomes a named fix (an issue or a charter change for the owner).

change_log.what: the thirteen rows of the 2026-10-18 elite-panel review, their measurable inputs, the code rules and the grade scale; the baseline letters are owner-only (training_constraints / RETRO#2026-10-18), never in this file

grade_scale.rule: a row score is 0-10; the letter is the highest row whose `min` the score reaches. The scale refines config/panel_rubric.json's letters (A, A-, B+ share their floors; B, C and D are each split into a plus/plain/minus band inside the rubric's own band), so a row score and a panel seat score read on one scale. tests/test_block_retro_5079.py holds the refinement.

combine_rule: a row's score is the mean of its code score (the mean of its measured code_rules) and the panel's median seat score; with only one of the two it is that one; with neither the row is `ungraded` and carries its last grade, said so. The session may override a row only with a recorded reason (block_retro.apply_overrides).

baseline.store: the letters are owner-only: USER#matthew#SOURCE#training_constraints / RETRO#2026-10-18 (kind baseline), written once by `scripts/training_block_retro.py baseline --apply` from the private review; the first retro reads it as its prior. No grade letter belongs in this file.

rows.label: Response to the 10 Oct event (reference only)
rows.note: The baseline graded how the plan and the coaching responded to one past interruption. A later block grades the response to any interruption inside it (the disruption-mode records, the step back up); a block with none carries the grade forward and raises no fix.
